title: Incident Response Apprenticeship & Evidence Lab
author: Priya Singh
content:
Overview:
This document defines a reproducible apprenticeship for new oncall responders and a standardized evidence-lab process for collecting forensic artifacts during LLM-serving incidents. It combines a staged training curriculum with concrete runbook exercises, an evidence checklist scoped to model serving (KV caches, token traces, model eval diffs), and templated customer and status-page messaging. The goal is to reduce time-to-competence for junior responders and improve the fidelity of post-incident analysis by ensuring consistent artifact capture.

Scope:
- Applies to all responders operating Redwood inference-hosted and dedicated clusters (hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments under Redwood ops support).
- Exercises include performance degradations, model-quality regressions, capacity saturation, quota-related throttles, and multi-region failover.
- Does NOT replace existing critical-runbooks (use those for immediate remediation). This training sits alongside runbook library and augments evidence capture.

Key outcomes:
- New responder reaches "independent responder" (can run triage, operate bridge, and capture required evidence) within 6 supervised incidents or 4 game days.
- Post-incident files include a verified evidence bundle with logs, traces, tokenized model outputs, snapshot of eval-run prompts, and SLO telemetry.

Roles and responsibilities:
1) Apprentice (new oncall trainee):
   - Observe 2 live incidents before active participation.
   - Run the Evidence Checklist during supervised incidents.
2) Mentor (senior oncall or SRE):
   - Provide live guidance, review apprentice evidence bundles, and sign-off on competency milestones.
3) Bridge Operator:
   - Operates incident bridge, leads comms cadence, and coordinates customer status updates.
4) Incident Commander (IC):
   - Drives restoration decisions, approves rollbacks and safety gates, owns postmortem assignment.

Apprenticeship curriculum (stages):
- Stage 0: Orientation (reading + self-paced labs)
  - Read: Incident process overview, runbook quick-start, status page policy.
  - Lab: Simulated alert walkthrough (1 hour).
- Stage 1: Shadowing (observe two incidents)
  - Focus: signal identification, evidence checklist familiarization.
- Stage 2: Guided response (mentor present)
  - Lead triage for low-severity events, capture evidence bundle, draft customer notice.
- Stage 3: Independent response (mentor on-call but not direct)
  - Lead medium-severity triage and bridge operations. Mentor reviews artifacts.
- Assessment: Practical exam during a scheduled game day scenario (see Game day design).

Incident intake & triage flow (compact):
1) Alert ingestion and enrichment:
   - Automatic enrichers attach: alerting_rule, service_owner, last_deploy, recent_rollout_tags, and model_version.
2) Initial classifier (5 mins):
   - Confirm: impact (internal svc only / customer-facing), affected regions, model(s) implicated.
   - If SLO breach or >5% customer request failures -> escalate to Bridge.
3) Evidence capture (first 10 mins): run Evidence Checklist.
4) Containment vs. Remediation plan (IC decision):
   - Contain: throttles, route to fallback model variant, capacity scale-up.
   - Remediate: diagnostics, model rollback, configuration tweak.

Evidence Checklist (must be attached to incident before bridge close):
- Time-windowed logs (service logs, orchestrator events) covering -5m to +30m around alert.
- Traces (sampled spans) for top 5 p99 requests by latency.
- Metrics snapshot: p50/p90/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, enqueue depth, KV cache hit-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, host-level memory.
- KV cache diagnostics: top keys by size and miss-rate, cache eviction spikes.
- Model inference artifacts:
  - Tokenized model outputs for 10 representative requests (input, output tokens, temperature, model version, quantization profile).
  - Eval-set diffs: latest eval score and delta vs baseline (if available).
- Network / infra artifacts: netstat / iostat snippets or cloud provider instance events if applicable.
- Deployment context: last_deploy_commit, rollout-id, feature-flag state.
- Human notes: chronology, hypothesis, remediation actions, who executed them.

Forensics & chain-of-evidence guidance:
- Preserve: do not truncate original log files; copy a time-bounded slice to the incident bundle.
- Signing: bundle owner (IC or Bridge Op) must add a small memo with the list of files and SHA256 checksums. Example: sha256sum incident-2025-02-01-evidence.tar.gz
- Access controls: mark evidence bundles as restricted in the incident tracker if they contain customer PII or redact per Data Handling policy.

Sample runbook excerpt: KV cache saturation (novel LLM-serving specifics)
- Trigger: alert if KV_cache_miss_rate > 20% AND p99 latency > 2s for 5 continuous minutes.
- Priority: P1 (customer-impacting).
- Immediate steps:
  1) Run: rbctl cache inspect --service=model-infer --window=10m --top=50 > /tmp/kv-top.txt
  2) Check cache eviction log: curl -sS https://ops-api.local/cache/events?since=10m | jq .
  3) If eviction spike present, increase cache capacity (temporary): infra-autoscaler scale cache-pool --replicas +1 --reason "KV-surge"
  4) If increase not possible, route traffic to smaller window model variant: routing-cli set-route --service model-infer --variant model-v2-small --weight 100 --reason "fallback due to KV saturation"
- Capture evidence: attach rbctl outputs, cache-top, eviction events, and the routing change audit log.

Customer and status page message templates (concise examples):
- Initial public status (short):
  Title: "Degradation: text-generation latency elevated in us-west-2"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated latency affecting text generation API in us-west-2. Impact: increased response times and occasional timeouts. Mitigation: routing to fallback variant and scaling. Next update: 30 minutes."
- Intermediate update (medium):
  Title: "Mitigation in progress: fallback routing and capacity increases applied"
  Body: "We have applied fallback routing to model-v2-small and increased Dedicated cache capacity. Error rates have reduced from 6% -> 2.1%. We are continuing diagnostics; ETA for full restoration: 2 hours. Customers on Dedicated will see reduced throughput while safety checks run."
- Full resolution notice (detailed):
  Title: "Resolved: latency normalized"
  Body: "Root cause: KV cache eviction surge due to a malformed batch workload after a merchant rollout. Mitigations: roll back merchant rollout, increased cache pool temporarily, and deployed a request-size validation gate. We collected a full evidence bundle. If you saw degraded outputs, please open a support ticket quoting incident ID. Post-incident review scheduled: YYYY-MM-DD."

Example Slack bridge snippets and automation:
- Automated first-ack (bot): "INCIDENT [INC-2025-0123] acknowledged: KV cache miss spike in us-west-2. Bridge: #inc-2025-0123. Initial triage started by @bridge-op."
- Manual bridge post (template): "Status: Mitigating. Action: Fallback routing to model-v2-small applied at 15:03 UTC. Observed: p99 latency down from 2.6s to 1.1s. Next: Observe for 20m then decide rollback."

Game day exercise design (assessment-style):
- Objective: Validate apprentice's ability to run triage, collect evidence, operate the bridge for 30–60 minutes, and produce a customer-facing timeline.
- Scenario examples:
  1) Synthetic traffic spike with malformed batch payloads causing cache churn.
  2) Silent regression: small eval delta (5%) in reranking model leading to increased user complaints (requires correlation between KL eval drop and downstream error rate).
- Scoring rubric (pass thresholds):
  - Evidence completeness: 80%+ items present (pass)
  - Time-to-initial-bridge (under escalation): < 8 minutes (pass)
  - Customer message clarity: reviewer score >= 4/5 (pass)
  - Root-cause hypothesis & remediation proposal: feasible and safety-aware (pass)
